edition.alertText: US conducts 'minor strikes' on Qeshm Island air defenses — first attacks since midterms; Trump says target destroyed in 15 minutes; Iran claims MQ-9 drone shot down over Qeshm; IRGC lifts missile range limits — says 2,000km cap 'no longer applies'; Iran army says Hormuz stays closed until all 7 conditions met; Qatar submits 48-hour peace plan: Stage 1 US lifts blockade + IAEA access, Stage 2 Hormuz reopens — neither side accepts; Araghchi calls 12 foreign ministers in 48 hours including Saudi, UAE, Qatar, Oman, Turkey, Pakistan; Brent settles $98.32, virtually flat (+0.03%) — down 16% for the week, steepest weekly drop since 2020; gold falls to $4,045 (-1.05%) on strong US jobs report (165K vs 65K expected) — Dec Fed hike odds 77-80%; WTI at $90.83; UKMTO reports 11 ships attacked in week ending Nov 6, three sank; MT Velos Sapphire hit by missile — 1 crew killed; IMO: 25 seafarers killed, 130 attacks since war began; Stephen Miller named White House chief of staff; Rezaei delivers Khamenei message to Putin in Moscow; Russia to supply Iran helicopter-mounted missile launchers (FT); Turkey ratifies Makkah Defence Pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan; US Treasury sanctions 8 Canada-based firms aiding Iran sanctions evasion via crypto; CENTCOM offers $20M reward for Iran nuclear info; US expands naval blockade to disrupt ground transport; Iran distributing iodine tablets near nuclear sites; Rapidan Energy sees 80% odds fighting resumes; US gas ~$4.04/gal

situation: The Strait of Hormuz crisis entered day 253 as the United States conducted fresh strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island — the first military action since the midterm elections four days earlier. Trump described the Friday strikes as 'minor,' saying the US had 'knocked out' an anti-aircraft device in roughly 15 minutes. Iranian state media reported two missile impacts in the Suza area of Qeshm, while the army claimed an MQ-9 drone was shot down over the island. In a significant escalation of rhetoric, IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi announced that Iran's 2,000-kilometer missile range limit 'has been lifted,' and Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei reportedly ordered unrestrained military response to any future threats. Iran's army spokesman Brigadier General Mohammad Akraminia declared that Hormuz would stay closed until the US accepts all seven conditions — including ending the naval blockade, lifting sanctions, releasing frozen assets, and paying war reparations. Despite the military tension, Qatar submitted a 48-hour peace plan on November 6: Stage 1 would require the US to lift its port blockade and grant IAEA access to nuclear facilities; Stage 2 would see Iran reopen Hormuz and commit to nuclear negotiations. Neither Washington nor Tehran has formally accepted. Trump told reporters 'we are dealing with them now — they want to make a deal' and claimed 'a lot of progress,' while Foreign Minister Araghchi said he had spoken with 12 foreign ministers in 48 hours, including counterparts from Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Oman, Turkey, and Pakistan. The appointment of Stephen Miller as White House chief of staff was read as a signal that Trump may not be ready to end the war, while Rapidan Energy's Bob McNally told CNBC he sees an 80% probability that fighting resumes. Turkey ratified the Makkah Defence Pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, formalizing the mutual defense alliance signed in August.

Oil markets ended a tumultuous week with Brent crude settling at $98.32 on November 6, essentially flat (+$0.03, +0.03%) as fresh Qeshm strikes and continued tanker attacks offset lingering ceasefire hopes from the Democratic midterm sweep. For the week, Brent plunged more than 16% from $117.64 — its steepest weekly decline since 2020. WTI settled at $90.83 (+$0.31, +0.34%), down nearly 13% for the week. Gold retreated to $4,045/oz (-1.05%) as a blowout October jobs report — 165,000 new positions versus 65,000 expected — pushed the dollar index up 0.72% to 102.28 and lifted December Fed rate hike odds to 77-80%. The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.87%. Newcastle coal eased to $144.45/tonne (-0.52%) as the broader energy complex continued adjusting to volatile ceasefire expectations. VLCC fixtures for Arabian Gulf routes edged higher on the Qeshm strikes, with AG-China rates estimated in the $420K-460K/day range as war-risk premiums rebounded from the midterm-driven lows. The EIA's October outlook put its fourth-quarter Brent forecast at $105, while Trading Economics forecasts $100.92 by year-end. US gasoline fell to approximately $4.04/gal (AAA), with GasBuddy's Patrick De Haan predicting prices could fall below $4 by next week. US diesel stood at $6.21/gal.

The maritime situation remained severe as UKMTO reported at least 11 ships attacked in and around the Strait of Hormuz in the week ending November 6, with three vessels sinking — bringing the estimated wartime sinking total to 14. The Greek-managed tanker MT Velos Sapphire was struck by a suspected missile in the Persian Gulf on November 5, killing one crew member. The International Maritime Organization reported that 25 seafarers have been killed and 130 attacks on commercial vessels recorded in Hormuz since the war began. A Western military intelligence agency has logged 88 projectile strikes since hostilities resumed in early July, but acknowledges most attacks go unreported. Vessel transits were running approximately 65% below pre-conflict levels, with many ships using a southern route near Oman with tracking systems disabled to move oil out. Iran has granted Hormuz transit exemptions to India, China, Iraq, and Qatar. The IRGC continued claiming mine strikes, reporting that a tanker with its transponder off caught fire after hitting a mine in the eastern Strait on November 6. The US expanded its naval blockade to include a task force dedicated to disrupting ground transport of Iranian oil. CENTCOM offered a $20 million reward for information about Iran's nuclear program, including its facilities, equipment, and personnel. Mohsen Rezaei delivered a message from Supreme Leader Khamenei to Putin in Moscow, and the Financial Times reported that Russia agreed to supply Iran with 90 helicopter-mounted missile launchers and has shared nuclear-relevant information. Saudi Arabia intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Najran and a drone near Mecca, while the Houthis accused the Saudi coalition of striking a market in Taiz governorate killing more than 30 people. The US Treasury sanctioned eight Canada-based currency exchange businesses accused of helping Iran evade sanctions through crypto activity linked to the IRGC. Iran was reported to be distributing iodine tablets near nuclear sites amid fears of a US strike on Pickaxe Mountain.

supplyChain.name: Sulfur
supplyChain.text: Global exports down 39% YoY to 6.1M tonnes in Q2 (S&P). Sulfur prices above $1,000/tonne — more than doubled since pre-war — feeding into phosphate production costs; Egypt, Brazil, India cutting output. Mosaic phosphate plants remain curtailed including South Fort Meade (Florida) — 199 workers laid off. Morocco's OCP needs 3.7M tonnes/yr from the region. Nearly half of seaborne sulfur passed through Hormuz pre-war. Phosphate prices up 25-30%. Trade routes shifting as Morocco and China seek alternative sources (ChemAnalyst).

supplyChain.name: Sulfuric Acid
supplyChain.text: China banned exports Apr-Aug (700kt/yr quota replaced). SX-EW copper producers (15% of global cathode) fully exposed. Huayou cut Indonesian nickel HPAL output 50%.

supplyChain.name: Fertilizer
supplyChain.text: Fertilizer shipments through Hormuz at zero for fourth consecutive month — September, October, and early November all zero (World Visualized/Syz Group/Fertilizer Daily). Urea exports from Hormuz-dependent economies fell 83% YoY in April (ITC). ~850kt urea stranded. 4 of 5 Bangladesh urea plants shut since March due to LNG shortages. Pakistan faces 200,000-ton fertiliser shortfall (Express Tribune). FAO Food Price Index at 136 (highest since Nov 2022). World Bank: fertilizer prices surging as Hormuz disruptions tighten supplies. India building two fertiliser futures — diversifying sources while lobbying for corridor (Diplomat Magazine). Urea-to-corn ratio at 126 bushels/tonne vs 75 in Dec 2025 (CSIS). IFPRI: no bypass route for ammonia or sulfur unlike crude. UN fertilizer corridor stalled pending US-Iran agreement. Hormuz crude recovery hides slower one for LNG, fertilizer, helium and aluminum — non-oil flows still near zero (Enterprise AM). Out of Hormuz energy shocks, the ingredients for a global food crisis intensify (PRNewswire/IFA).

supplyChain.name: LNG
supplyChain.text: QatarEnergy extends LNG force majeure through end of December 2026 — 8th consecutive extension since April. Global LNG supply gap estimated at ~600 bcf. Dutch TTF gas at €97.53/MWh (~$108.51), highest since 2022 energy crisis. Pakistan to pay >$1B for winter LNG spot cargoes at ~2x Qatari contract price. Qatari LNG carrier Al Mayeda struck near Hormuz (Oct 31). Bangladesh struggling with spot market costs. Lufthansa says 2026 fuel costs €2B higher amid Iran war; group bars crew overnight stays in Israel through Nov 30. Europe and Asia face tight supply heading into winter. JERA CEO says Qatar LNG supply unlikely to recover soon.

supplyChain.name: Petrochemicals
supplyChain.text: MEG ethylene/polyethylene exports disrupted. Gulf petrochem complex cut to ~60% capacity. Methanol down 80% (ITC). Dow, LyondellBasell margins widening on supply constraint. ExxonMobil Q3 profit more than doubled to $15.4B on energy surge. Aramco Q3 profit surges 34.6% to $36.3B.
